clue.text: Native American has a vehicle back at house

indicators.note: back tells us to read the little phrase 'a vehicle' from right to left

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A Native American owns a car parked behind their home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the opening pair of pieces round, so the vehicle comes before the A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Navaho (also spelt Navajo) are a people of the south-western United States, so the name fits a Native American.

clue.text: Joe's not right in the head — this to fix part of it?

definitions.text: this to fix part of it

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the word for the head

parts.note: nob is old slang for the head

indicators.note: not right suggests the letters of the name are out of order and need rearranging

parts.note: the name with its S, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Joe seems a bit odd in the head, and the clue wonders whether surgery might fix part of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' scrambles the name, and 'in' places the scramble after the first letter of the slang head. The definition plays on 'part of it', the head, and the question mark flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinoplasty, cosmetic surgery on the nose, is an operation to fix one part of the head.

clue.text: Money raised: a little bit at the end stolen out of spite

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is written bottom to top

indicators.text: a little bit at the end stolen
indicators.note: the final letter loses a little bit, its tail stroke, so a Y drawn without its tail turns into a V

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone resents money being collected while a small sum went missing at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: A visual trick: rub out the tail of the Y at the end of MONEY and it looks like a V, giving MONEV; 'raised' then turns it upwards, so it reads VENOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom is bitter malice in speech or manner, a close synonym of spite.

clue.text: In big house, working to hold small celebration

parts.note: a hall is a large country house

indicators.note: to hold means one piece sits inside another, as if held

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
wee is Scots for small

explanation.surface: A modest party is held at a working country mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is only a link word, not a container signal; the containment comes from 'to hold'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowe'en, 31 October, is a festival marked by costumes and parties, so it is a celebration.

clue.text: See 19 down
Heard rumour, some whispered into this?

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Gossip overheard, with some of it murmured privately into someone's ear.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a whisper goes into the ear, reaching this membrane; the question mark flags the loose sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A whisper is spoken into the ear, and the membrane it reaches inside is what the definition describes, by example.

clue.text: Favour partner for girl

definitions.meaning: in the fixed phrase '... and favour', this is the word that partners favour

explanation.surface: Someone asks a favour: finding a partner for a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: A grace-and-favour home in Britain is one given rent-free by the Crown, so the word sits beside 'favour'. 'for' just links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: It pairs with favour in a set British phrase, and it is also a common woman's first name.

clue.text: Humiliating condition, rudest I've suffered

indicators.note: suffered implies the words were put through damage and come out in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone complains of the most humiliating rudeness they have ever had to endure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffered' rearranges the nine letters of RUDEST IVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Servitude is bondage or forced subjection to another, a demeaning state to live in.

clue.text: Not easy to identify, childishly made to go round the bend

indicators.note: to go round means the outer word is wrapped about the other piece

parts.note: a small child regularises the verb and says 'maked' for made
an S-bend, so a bend can be the letter S

explanation.surface: Someone driven mad in a childish way becomes hard to recognise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go round the bend' looks like going mad, but here the child's form MAKED goes round S, the bend, giving MA-S-KED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wearing a mask is disguised, and so is hard to recognise.

clue.text: Sample of the West Country praying?

parts.note: the south-west of England, abbreviated SW
someone praying is at church, AT plus CH, the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A quaint picture of someone from England's south-west at prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Country is south-west England (Cornwall, Devon, Somerset). 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A swatch is a small piece of fabric shown to a customer, a sample of the material.

clue.text: Summer plant beginning to fade, during sign of winter's approach

indicators.note: during says one piece comes in the middle of the other

parts.note: as winter nears, the sun is lower in the sky

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A summer bloom starts to wilt as winter draws in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign of winter's approach' looks like frost or falling leaves, but means the sun sitting lower in the sky; 'beginning to' and 'during' place the F between its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall yellow-headed Helianthus blooms in summer, so it is a summer plant.

clue.text: Large area of a sort of moon reduced by half

indicators.note: reduced by half means the word loses the back half of its letters

parts.note: a crescent is the shape of the moon when only a sliver shows

explanation.surface: A wide expanse, half lit like a crescent moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced by half' cuts CRESCENT to its first four letters, CRES. 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Acres is a common informal way of saying a great expanse, as in acres of space.

clue.text: Huge job's ending after half one month and during second

indicators.note: after says the final letter of the job comes following the shortened month
half says only part of the month's name is kept, here its first two letters

parts.note: June is a month

indicators.note: during places that letter in the middle of the word for a second

parts.note: mo, as in 'half a mo', is a moment or second

indicators.note: ending picks the last letter of the word for a job

explanation.surface: An enormous task to finish mid-month, within a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps the first two letters of the month; the B from 'ending' sits both 'after' those and 'during' the word for a second.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo, from the famous elephant, means very large, as in a jumbo jet.

clue.text: Disaster once, but league more or less keeps one secure

indicators.note: keeps means the outer phrase holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a league is an old measure of roughly three miles
I is the Roman numeral one
to land something, like a contract or a fish, is to secure it

explanation.surface: A past calamity, yet a league roughly preserves someone's security.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' puts I inside THREE MILES, between the E and the S, giving THREE MILE IS, then LAND follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1979 partial meltdown at the Pennsylvania nuclear plant was a notable past catastrophe.

clue.text: Points taken in something copper has to say in pleading

indicators.note: taken in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the copper beech is a tree, so a copper has a beech
S and E are two compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: A police officer, with points on their record, has something to plead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer but is the tree variety, the copper beech. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech is to ask urgently and earnestly, which is exactly what someone does when pleading.

clue.text: Desist, Tea Party, in America!

indicators.note: a party is a lively free-for-all, so the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A plea to the Tea Party, the US conservative movement, to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks part of the political name but is the anagram signal. The Tea Party is an American political movement, so the surface sits in the right country.
explanation.definitionFit: Stateside is an adverb meaning in or towards the United States, used by people outside it.

clue.text: Make attempt to avoid woodwork

indicators.note: to avoid means the inlay word is written without the attempt

parts.note: marquetry is decorative inlaid woodwork
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone tries hard to keep clear of carpentry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' looks like a verb but is a noun, a brand of car.
explanation.definitionFit: A marque is a brand of product, especially of car, which is what 'make' means as a noun.

clue.text: So busy, unable to get decent jogging gear?

definitions.meaning: exhausted by having far too much to do

definitions.text: unable to get decent jogging gear
definitions.meaning: a jogger left in tatty, torn kit, read literally

explanation.surface: A runner too frantic to buy proper running clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the idiom literally: a runner in rags.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means worn out from constant demands, so someone that busy fits; a jogger dressed in rags fits literally.

clue.text: Stone fish trap

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
a net is a trap for fish

explanation.surface: A rock used as a trap for fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Garnet is a deep red gem, a precious or semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Guided tour taken in the wrong order gets hugely extended

indicators.note: the two pieces are written in the opposite order from the clue's

parts.note: a trip is a tour
led means guided

explanation.surface: A guided tour taken backwards ends up far longer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in the wrong order' swaps the two pieces from the order the clue gives them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tripled has grown threefold, a large expansion.

clue.text: Give up attic, once delightful housing

indicators.note: housing means the words contain the answer, holding it inside them

explanation.surface: Someone surrenders the attic that was once lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' signals the letters inside ATTIC ONCE DELIGHTFUL, starting at the C of attic.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede is to admit defeat or yield, so it means to give up.

clue.text: Why I must be erotic, go-go dancing: to get a quantity of money

indicators.note: dancing means the letters move around into a new arrangement

parts.note: the two words of the hyphenated term, taken letter by letter
a sum is an amount of money

explanation.surface: A go-go dancer insists on being sexy because it pays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges EROTIC GOGO; 'to get' is a link. The Latin is Descartes's 'I think, therefore I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: Descartes's proof of existence states the reason he must exist: because he thinks.

clue.text: Publicly support salesmen, not very effectively at first

indicators.note: not tells us the abbreviation for very is removed

parts.note: vendors are people who sell

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A sales team gives public backing, though ineffectively at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not very' looks like a qualifier but takes V out of VENDORS, and 'at first' adds E from 'effectively'.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse something is to declare approval of it in public, as a celebrity backs a product.

clue.text: See 12
Small drink failing to be calming

parts.note: tea is a drink
something failing is dying

explanation.surface: A little drink fails to soothe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadying means making steady or settling, which is calming someone or something.

clue.text: Handed out cards, dropping a letter

indicators.note: in a down clue, dropping moves a letter further down the column, here to the end

parts.note: dealt means handed out cards

explanation.surface: Someone deals the cards and lets one fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping a' moves the A in DEALT down to the bottom, giving DELT-A. 'letter' looks like a mailed note.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Was not resting, but took steps

definitions.meaning: 'resting' is an actor's word for being out of work, so this means having a part

explanation.surface: Someone stopped resting and went into action.
explanation.walkthrough: Actors say they are 'resting' when unemployed. 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing on stage is the opposite of an actor's resting, and also means took action.

clue.text: Pharaoh is up-and-coming African

parts.note: Tut is short for Tutankhamun, the boy pharaoh

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' says the word is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A young pharaoh is a rising African star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up-and-coming' turns IS upwards in this down clue, giving SI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are a people of Rwanda and Burundi, so a Tutsi is an African.

clue.text: For speaking, one that receives part in Shakespeare

indicators.note: for speaking says the word must be pronounced, and a word of like sound is meant

parts.note: an aerial is a device that picks up broadcast signals

explanation.surface: An actor takes a speaking role in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' looks like a piece, but it is a role. Ariel is the airy spirit in The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is a role in The Tempest, the spirit Prospero commands.

clue.text: Set fire to one reptile in sewer, according to reports

definitions.note: a sewer, pronounced like 'suer', is one who sues

parts.note: lit means set fire to
I is the Roman numeral one
gator is short for alligator

explanation.surface: Someone sets an alligator alight in the drains, as the urban legend of sewer alligators goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' looks like a drain but 'according to reports' says to hear it as 'suer'; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A litigator is a party bringing a lawsuit, one who sues.

clue.text: Reactionary has special hide-away

indicators.note: special suggests the letters are rearranged into an unusual form

parts.note: read as A plus WAY, and RD (road) is a way

explanation.surface: A conservative owns an exclusive hidden retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide-away' looks like one word, but 'special' rearranges HIDE to DIEH and 'away' is A WAY, A plus RD. 'has' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A die-hard is someone stubbornly resisting change, a staunch conservative or reactionary.

clue.text: Piece of asparagus cut round very tip

indicators.note: a piece of the word is its opening letter
round means the word for cut surrounds the other piece

parts.note: to dice food is to cut it into cubes

explanation.surface: Kitchen guidance: chop asparagus around the spear's tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' looks like the end of the asparagus but is the definition. 'round' puts V in DICE after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip is a helpful hint or suggestion, which is a piece of advice.
